context_requirements: Fungal target (e.g., ergosterol biosynthesis, fungal cell membrane, fungal DNA) must be present; human cells lack the intended antifungal target
DNMT1 engagement in human cells would require the drug to be a bona fide DNMT1 inhibitor at 10 micromolar, which is not established for this class
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine human lines
A shared transcriptional signature across lines consistent with DNMT1 inhibition (e.g., DNA methylation-related gene changes)
Evidence of DNA damage response or apoptosis induction in human lines at 10 micromolar

changes: Removed all retrieved abstracts: none report a human-cell transcriptional experiment at 10 micromolar in the nine listed lines, and none support DNMT1 as the target of an 'other antifungal' mechanism.
PMID 41817161 concerns paroxetine/fluoxetine against Candida spp.; it does not establish DNMT1 inhibition or a human-cell transcriptional signature.
PMID 32457728 concerns palmitic acid antivirulence effects on Candida tropicalis; it does not support DNMT1 as a target or any human-cell response.
PMID 24060867 concerns berberine/fluconazole synergy in Candida albicans via cell-cycle effects; it does not support DNMT1 inhibition in human cells.
PMID 21807970 concerns an ApoE-derived antifungal peptide in Candida albicans; it does not support DNMT1 as a target or human-cell transcriptional changes.
Kept primary_targets as DNMT1 only because the input hypothesis asserts it, but flagged in context_requirements that this is not established for the antifungal class at 10 micromolar.
Kept all gene lists empty because no direction, specificity, line-response, kinetics, or magnitude claims were made in the input hypothesis.
